rubric.why: Identifies piracy as unauthorized copying or distribution of protected material.
rubric.description: States that the copying or distribution is unauthorized.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning unauthorized copying or distribution.

rubric.why: Identifies that online piracy involves digital material shared through the internet.
rubric.description: Links the act to digital content and the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying digital content shared online.

modelAnswer: Online piracy is the unauthorized copying or distribution of copyrighted digital material through the internet.
Examples include illegally sharing movies, music, software, or e-books online.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a computer virus and a computer worm?

rubric.why: Shows that a hacker is a person or individual.
rubric.description: Defines a hacker as a person who uses computer skills to access or affect computer systems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a hacker as a person.

rubric.why: Distinguishes hacking as an action or process, not a person.
rubric.description: Defines hacking as the act of gaining access to or manipulating a computer system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying hacking as an activity or process.

modelAnswer: A hacker is a person who uses computer skills to access or affect computer systems.
Hacking is the activity or process of gaining access to or manipulating a computer system.

items.followUp: Write HTML code to display the ordered list: 1. Apple 2. Mango.

rubric.why: Shows the ordered-list structure and begins a list item.
rubric.description: Uses an ordered-list tag and a list-item tag for BISE.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly using <ol> and a <li> element.

rubric.why: Includes the second item and closes the list.
rubric.description: Adds FBIS as the second item and closes the ordered list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including FBIS and the closing list tag.

modelAnswer: <ol>
• BISE
• FBIS

items.followUp: Write an HTML tag for setting a webpage background colour.

rubric.why: Identifies the body tag and its background-image attribute.
rubric.description: Uses the background attribute in the body tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct tag and attribute.

rubric.why: Shows that an image file is specified as the background.
rubric.description: Provides an image filename as the attribute value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying a background image file.

modelAnswer: Use the background attribute in the opening <body> tag and give it the image file name.
Example: <body background="image.jpg">

items.followUp: What is the difference between an opening tag and a closing tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies the first tag in a paired-tag structure.
rubric.description: States that a paired tag has an opening or start tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the opening tag.

rubric.why: Identifies the second tag in a paired-tag structure.
rubric.description: States that a paired tag has a closing or end tag, which uses a slash.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the closing tag and its slash.

modelAnswer: A paired tag consists of an opening tag and a closing tag.
The opening tag starts the element, and the closing tag, written with a slash, ends it; the content is placed between them.
Example: Text

items.followUp: Name and explain the flowchart symbols for input/output and decision.

rubric.why: Identifies the terminal symbol and its purpose.
rubric.description: Explains the oval symbol used for the start or end of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct shape and function.

rubric.why: Identifies the input/output symbol and its purpose.
rubric.description: Explains that a parallelogram represents input or output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct shape and function.

rubric.why: Identifies the processing symbol and its purpose.
rubric.description: Explains that a rectangle represents a processing step or calculation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct shape and function.

rubric.why: Identifies the decision symbol and its purpose.
rubric.description: Explains that a diamond represents a decision or condition with branches.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct shape and function.

modelAnswer: Oval (terminal): shows the start or end of the algorithm.
Parallelogram (input/output): shows data entering or leaving the algorithm.
Rectangle (process): shows an instruction or calculation.
Diamond (decision): shows a condition that leads to alternative paths, such as Yes/No.

items.followUp: Explain resource sharing in a computer network and give two examples.

rubric.why: Defines file sharing as access to or exchange of files between networked computers.
rubric.description: Explains that users can share or access files over a network.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for describing network-based file access or exchange.

rubric.why: Gives an example of the type of material shared.
rubric.description: Names examples such as documents or data files.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant file example.

rubric.why: Shows a practical way shared files are stored or accessed.
rubric.description: Mentions a shared folder or centrally stored files accessible to users.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid shared-storage detail.

modelAnswer: File sharing allows users on a computer network to access or exchange files stored on another computer.
Users can share documents, data, and other files through a shared network folder or server.
It allows several users to use the same files without making separate copies on each computer.

items.followUp: Explain how sharing a printer on a network is useful.

rubric.why: Defines hardware sharing as making devices available to multiple computers on a network.
rubric.description: Explains that network users can access hardware connected to another computer or the network.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for describing shared access to network hardware.

rubric.why: Provides a relevant example of shared hardware.
rubric.description: Names a device such as a printer, scanner, or storage device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable hardware example.

rubric.why: Identifies a practical benefit of hardware sharing.
rubric.description: Explains that sharing reduces the need for a separate device for every computer or allows several users to use it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid benefit.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing allows several computers on a network to use the same hardware device.
Devices such as printers, scanners, and storage devices can be shared.
This reduces the cost of buying a separate device for every computer and makes the device available to multiple users.
